forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: c180
+title: 'Review tool: `get rules` op — the rules that apply to a target file, via the engine matcher'
+---
+# Goal
+
+An implementer must get the rules for a file before it edits the file. The response must equal what a review run will enforce.
+
+# Problem today
+
+- `list validators` accepts a `match` filter, but `passes_filters` (crates/swissarmyhammer-tools/src/mcp/tools/review/validators.rs:131) reimplements the matching. It diverges from the engine in two ways:
+  1. A validator with no `match.files` globs matches every file in the engine (`matches_files`, crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/validators/types.rs:372) but the tool filter excludes it (empty compiled globs never match).
+  2. The substring test `globs.iter().any(|g| g.contains(needle))` reports validators the engine would not run.
+- The summaries carry no rule bodies. To read the rules for one file, an agent must call `get validator` once per validator.
+
+# Changes
+
+1. Add op `get rules` to the review tool:
+   - Input: `path` — one repo-relative file path, or an array of paths.
+   - Pairing: `MatchContext::new().with_file(path)` → `loader.matching_rulesets(&ctx)` — the same call the scope stage uses (`match_validators_and_files`, crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/scope.rs:434). Do not compile globs in the tool layer.
+   - Output: for each matched ruleset — `name`, `description` (mandate), `source_layer`, and each rule `name` + `body` verbatim. For an array input, report each ruleset once with the paths it matched.
+2. Fix `passes_filters`: when `match` is given, delegate to `loader.matching_rulesets` with a `MatchContext` for that path. Remove the substring test.
+3. Register the op in the review tool dispatch and its schema/description text.
+
+# Acceptance
+
+- A production-path test: for a `.rs` path, the `get rules` ruleset set equals the set `match_validators_and_files` pairs for the same path.
+- A test: a ruleset without `match.files` appears for every path.
+- Rule bodies in the response are verbatim from the loaded rules.
+- `cargo nextest run -E 'rdeps(swissarmyhammer-tools)'` passes.
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -3,31 +3,24 @@
 - claude-code
 position_column: todo
 position_ordinal: c180
-title: 'Review tool: `get rules` op — the rules that apply to a target file, via the engine matcher'
+title: 'Review tool: `list validators` returns rule bodies on request (`rules: true`)'
 ---
 # Goal

-An implementer must get the rules for a file before it edits the file. The response must equal what a review run will enforce.
+One call gets the full rules that apply to a target file. This supports the implement skill: read the rules for a file before you edit the file.

-# Problem today
+# What works today (verified live)

-- `list validators` accepts a `match` filter, but `passes_filters` (crates/swissarmyhammer-tools/src/mcp/tools/review/validators.rs:131) reimplements the matching. It diverges from the engine in two ways:
-  1. A validator with no `match.files` globs matches every file in the engine (`matches_files`, crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/validators/types.rs:372) but the tool filter excludes it (empty compiled globs never match).
-  2. The substring test `globs.iter().any(|g| g.contains(needle))` reports validators the engine would not run.
-- The summaries carry no rule bodies. To read the rules for one file, an agent must call `get validator` once per validator.
+`{"op": "list validators", "match": "crates/swissarmyhammer-skills/src/skill_loader.rs"}` returns the correct 16 validators for a Rust file. The glob test is the engine's own `matches_any_pattern` + `GLOB_MATCH_OPTIONS`, and the loader defaults a missing `match:` to the source-code file group — so the answer agrees with the review engine for full-path queries. But the summaries carry only descriptions. To read the rule bodies, a caller must then call `get validator` once per name (16 calls for one Rust file).

 # Changes

-1. Add op `get rules` to the review tool:
-   - Input: `path` — one repo-relative file path, or an array of paths.
-   - Pairing: `MatchContext::new().with_file(path)` → `loader.matching_rulesets(&ctx)` — the same call the scope stage uses (`match_validators_and_files`, crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/scope.rs:434). Do not compile globs in the tool layer.
-   - Output: for each matched ruleset — `name`, `description` (mandate), `source_layer`, and each rule `name` + `body` verbatim. For an array input, report each ruleset once with the paths it matched.
-2. Fix `passes_filters`: when `match` is given, delegate to `loader.matching_rulesets` with a `MatchContext` for that path. Remove the substring test.
-3. Register the op in the review tool dispatch and its schema/description text.
+1. Add an optional boolean `rules` (default false) to `list validators` in the review tool (crates/swissarmyhammer-tools/src/mcp/tools/review/validators.rs). When true, each row also carries the ruleset's rules: each rule `name` + `body` verbatim (same shape as `get validator`).
+2. Keep the matching path unchanged — one call with `match: <file>` + `rules: true` returns the full rule text that a review run will enforce on that file.
+3. Update the tool description (description.md) with the new field and the implement-time use: get the rules for a file before you edit it.
+4. Alignment cleanup while there: in `passes_filters`, prefer the engine's `MatchContext` + `matching_rulesets` path for a path-shaped `match` value, so the tool can never drift from the engine matcher. Keep the documented lenient substring behavior for glob-fragment queries.

 # Acceptance

-- A production-path test: for a `.rs` path, the `get rules` ruleset set equals the set `match_validators_and_files` pairs for the same path.
-- A test: a ruleset without `match.files` appears for every path.
-- Rule bodies in the response are verbatim from the loaded rules.
+- A production-path test: `list validators` with `match: <a .rs path>` and `rules: true` returns the same ruleset names the engine pairs via `match_validators_and_files` for that path, each with verbatim rule bodies.
 - `cargo nextest run -E 'rdeps(swissarmyhammer-tools)'` passes.
\ No newline at end of file
